questions.prompt: An oscillator completes \(18\) cycles in \(9.0\,\mathrm{s}\). Find its frequency.
questions.answer:
Frequency is cycles per second:
\[
f=\frac{18}{9.0}=2.0\,\mathrm{Hz}
\]

questions.prompt: An oscillator has period \(0.25\,\mathrm{s}\). Find its frequency.
An oscillator has frequency \(0.50\,\mathrm{Hz}\). Find its period.
An oscillator has frequency \(5.0\,\mathrm{Hz}\). Find its angular frequency.
questions.answer:
\[
\omega=2\pi f=2\pi(5.0)=10\pi\,\mathrm{rad\,s^{-1}}
\]
Numerically, \(\omega\approx31.4\,\mathrm{rad\,s^{-1}}\).

questions.prompt: The maximum displacement from equilibrium is \(0.12\,\mathrm{m}\). What is the amplitude and what is the peak-to-peak displacement?
questions.answer:
The amplitude is measured from equilibrium, so
\[
A=0.12\,\mathrm{m}
\]
The peak-to-peak displacement is
\[
2A=0.24\,\mathrm{m}
\]

questions.prompt: An oscillator has angular frequency \(12\,\mathrm{rad\,s^{-1}}\). How much phase does it advance in \(0.50\,\mathrm{s}\)?
questions.answer:
Phase advance is
\[
\Delta\varphi=\omega\Delta t
\]
so
\[
\Delta\varphi=12(0.50)=6.0\,\mathrm{rad}
\]

questions.prompt: A periodic displacement is \(x(t)=0.30\cos(8\pi t)\,\mathrm{m}\). Find \(A\), \(\omega\), \(f\), and \(T\).
A sinusoidal oscillator has \(A=0.050\,\mathrm{m}\) and \(T=0.80\,\mathrm{s}\). Write one possible displacement function that starts at maximum positive displacement.
questions.answer:
Starting at maximum positive displacement means use cosine with \(\phi=0\). The angular frequency is
\[
\omega=\frac{2\pi}{T}=\frac{2\pi}{0.80}=2.5\pi\,\mathrm{rad\,s^{-1}}
\]
One model is
\[
x(t)=0.050\cos(2.5\pi t)\,\mathrm{m}
\]

questions.prompt: A motion has period \(1.6\,\mathrm{s}\). How many complete cycles occur in \(12.8\,\mathrm{s}\)?
questions.answer:
The number of cycles is
\[
N=\frac{\Delta t}{T}=\frac{12.8}{1.6}=8
\]

questions.prompt: Write a displacement model for an oscillator with amplitude \(0.20\,\mathrm{m}\), period \(4.0\,\mathrm{s}\), and \(x(0)=0.20\,\mathrm{m}\).
questions.answer:
Starting at maximum positive displacement gives a cosine with \(\phi=0\). The angular frequency is
\[
\omega=\frac{2\pi}{T}=\frac{2\pi}{4.0}=\frac{\pi}{2}\,\mathrm{rad\,s^{-1}}
\]
One model is
\[
x(t)=0.20\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2}t\right)\,\mathrm{m}
\]

questions.prompt: For \(x(t)=A\cos(\omega t+\phi)\), what phase constant \(\phi\) makes \(x(0)=0\) and the initial velocity negative?
questions.answer:
For \(x(0)=0\),
\[
A\cos\phi=0
\]
so \(\phi=\pi/2\) or \(3\pi/2\). Velocity is
\[
v(t)=-A\omega\sin(\omega t+\phi)
\]
so
\[
v(0)=-A\omega\sin\phi
\]
For \(v(0)<0\), \(\sin\phi>0\). Therefore
\[
\phi=\frac{\pi}{2}
\]

questions.prompt: For \(x(t)=A\cos(\omega t)\), find the first positive time when \(x=-A\).
questions.answer:
For \(x=A\cos(\omega t)\), the first time \(x=-A\) occurs when
\[
\cos(\omega t)=-1
\]
so
\[
\omega t=\pi
\]
and
\[
t=\frac{\pi}{\omega}=\frac{T}{2}
\]

questions.prompt: Two oscillations have the same amplitude and period. One is \(x_1=A\cos\omega t\), and the other reaches maximum displacement a quarter period later. Write \(x_2(t)\) in cosine form.
questions.answer:
A quarter-period delay corresponds to a phase lag of
\[
\omega\frac{T}{4}=\frac{2\pi}{T}\frac{T}{4}=\frac{\pi}{2}
\]
So one cosine form is
\[
x_2(t)=A\cos\left(\omega t-\frac{\pi}{2}\right)
\]
This reaches its maximum when \(\omega t-\pi/2=0\), at \(t=T/4\).

questions.prompt: An oscillator has \(x(0)=-A/2\) and \(v(0)>0\). Find \(\phi\) for \(x=A\cos(\omega t+\phi)\), with \(0\leq\phi<2\pi\).
questions.answer:
The initial displacement gives
\[
A\cos\phi=-\frac{A}{2}
\]
so
\[
\cos\phi=-\frac{1}{2}
\]
Candidates are
\[
\phi=\frac{2\pi}{3},\quad \frac{4\pi}{3}
\]
Velocity is
\[
v(0)=-A\omega\sin\phi
\]
For \(v(0)>0\), \(\sin\phi<0\). Therefore
\[
\phi=\frac{4\pi}{3}
\]

questions.prompt: Two identical sinusoidal oscillators have period \(T\). The second reaches every feature \(0.15T\) later than the first. Find its phase lag in radians.
questions.answer:
A delay \(\Delta t\) corresponds to phase lag
\[
\Delta\varphi=\omega\Delta t
\]
with
\[
\omega=\frac{2\pi}{T},\qquad \Delta t=0.15T
\]
so
\[
\Delta\varphi=\frac{2\pi}{T}(0.15T)=0.30\pi\,\mathrm{rad}
\]

questions.prompt: An oscillator is modeled by \(x(t)=A\cos(\omega t+\phi)\). It has \(x(0)=A/2\) and \(v(0)<0\). Find \(\phi\) in the range \(0\leq\phi<2\pi\).
questions.answer:
The initial displacement gives
\[
A\cos\phi=\frac{A}{2}
\]
so
\[
\cos\phi=\frac{1}{2}
\]
In the range \(0\leq\phi<2\pi\), the candidates are
\[
\phi=\frac{\pi}{3},\quad \frac{5\pi}{3}
\]
Velocity is
\[
v(0)=-A\omega\sin\phi
\]
For \(v(0)<0\), \(\sin\phi>0\), so
\[
\phi=\frac{\pi}{3}
\]

questions.prompt: An oscillator has \(A=0.060\,\mathrm{m}\), \(T=2.0\,\mathrm{s}\), \(x(0)=0.030\,\mathrm{m}\), and \(v(0)>0\). Construct \(x(t)=A\cos(\omega t+\phi)\).
questions.answer:
The angular frequency is
\[
\omega=\frac{2\pi}{T}=\pi\,\mathrm{rad\,s^{-1}}
\]
The initial displacement gives
\[
0.060\cos\phi=0.030
\]
so
\[
\cos\phi=\frac{1}{2}
\]
Candidates are \(\pi/3\) and \(5\pi/3\). Since
\[
v(0)=-A\omega\sin\phi
\]
and \(v(0)>0\), choose \(\sin\phi<0\):
\[
\phi=\frac{5\pi}{3}
\]
Thus
\[
x(t)=0.060\cos\left(\pi t+\frac{5\pi}{3}\right)\,\mathrm{m}
\]

questions.prompt: A sensor records successive positive maxima at \(t=0.30\,\mathrm{s}\), \(1.10\,\mathrm{s}\), and \(1.90\,\mathrm{s}\). The maximum displacement is \(0.040\,\mathrm{m}\). Construct a cosine model \(x(t)=A\cos(\omega t+\phi)\), choosing \(0\leq\phi<2\pi\), and state the timing assumptions.
questions.answer:
Successive positive maxima are separated by one period. The times differ by
\[
1.10-0.30=0.80\,\mathrm{s},\qquad 1.90-1.10=0.80\,\mathrm{s}
\]
so
\[
T=0.80\,\mathrm{s}
\]
and
\[
\omega=\frac{2\pi}{T}=2.5\pi\,\mathrm{rad\,s^{-1}}
\]
The amplitude is
\[
A=0.040\,\mathrm{m}
\]
For a positive maximum at \(t=0.30\,\mathrm{s}\),
\[
\omega(0.30)+\phi=2\pi n
\]
Choose \(n=1\):
\[
\phi=2\pi-(2.5\pi)(0.30)=2\pi-0.75\pi=1.25\pi=\frac{5\pi}{4}
\]
One model is
\[
x(t)=0.040\cos\left(2.5\pi t+\frac{5\pi}{4}\right)\,\mathrm{m}
\]
This assumes the recorded maxima are consecutive positive maxima and the motion is sinusoidal with constant period.

questions.prompt: A sinusoidal displacement has a positive-going equilibrium crossing at \(t=0.20\,\mathrm{s}\) and the next negative-going equilibrium crossing at \(t=0.70\,\mathrm{s}\). Its amplitude is \(0.090\,\mathrm{m}\). Construct \(x(t)=A\cos(\omega t+\phi)\), choosing \(0\leq\phi<2\pi\).
questions.answer:
A positive-going equilibrium crossing and the next negative-going equilibrium crossing are half a period apart, so
\[
\frac{T}{2}=0.70-0.20=0.50\,\mathrm{s}
\]
Thus
\[
T=1.0\,\mathrm{s},\qquad \omega=2\pi\,\mathrm{rad\,s^{-1}}
\]
At \(t=0.20\,\mathrm{s}\), the displacement is zero and velocity is positive. For cosine form, positive-going crossing requires phase \(3\pi/2\) modulo \(2\pi\):
\[
\omega(0.20)+\phi=\frac{3\pi}{2}
\]
\[
0.40\pi+\phi=\frac{3\pi}{2}
\]
\[
\phi=\frac{11\pi}{10}
\]
Therefore
\[
x(t)=0.090\cos\left(2\pi t+\frac{11\pi}{10}\right)\,\mathrm{m}
\]

questions.prompt: Two signals are \(x_1=A\cos(\omega t)\) and \(x_2=A\cos(\omega t+\phi)\). Derive all time shifts \(\Delta t\) for which \(x_2(t)=x_1(t+\Delta t)\), and explain why the answer is not unique.
questions.answer:
Require
\[
x_2(t)=x_1(t+\Delta t)
\]
so
\[
A\cos(\omega t+\phi)=A\cos(\omega t+\omega\Delta t)
\]
For the same signal for all \(t\), the phases must differ by an integer multiple of \(2\pi\):
\[
\omega\Delta t=\phi+2\pi n
\]
where \(n\) is any integer. Thus
\[
\Delta t=\frac{\phi+2\pi n}{\omega},\qquad n\in\mathbb{Z}
\]
The answer is not unique because adding one full period to a time shift gives the same sinusoidal signal.
